mainTopic: Does a נדר against ירק include דלועין? The dispute between the רבנן and רבי עקיבא about a שליח who has to check with his sender, and how that principle applies to a שליח who misuses הקדש.
overview: The משנה teaches that someone who vows off ירק may still eat דלועין, but רבי עקיבא forbids them. The רבנן try to prove their view from a messenger sent to buy vegetables, and רבי עקיבא turns the same example into proof for his side. The גמרא asks how a vow on 'vegetables' could include gourds. עולא explains that the person said 'a vegetable cooked in a pot.' The גמרא then states the principle behind the dispute: if a שליח has to check with his sender about an item, is it a different kind or the same kind? אביי adds that even רבי עקיבא would not give מלקות for eating gourds. The גמרא then quotes a משנה in מעילה: a שליח who switches meat and liver is himself guilty of מעילה. רב חסדא says this משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, and אביי begins to answer that it can, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: does a vow against vegetables include gourds?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who vows off ירק may eat דלועין, but רבי עקיבא forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who vowed not to eat vegetables may still eat gourds. רבי עקיבא says he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a dispute. The first opinion allows gourds after a vow against vegetables, and רבי עקיבא forbids them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows follow how people normally talk. The question is whether ordinary speakers count gourds as 'vegetables.' The first opinion (the רבנן) says they do not, and רבי עקיבא says they do.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes a vow (נדר) forbidding something to himself

phrases.english: One who vows off vegetables —
is permitted to eat gourds,
and Rabbi Akiva forbids them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against ירק does not forbid דלועין according to the רבנן. רבי עקיבא says it does.

steps.title: The רבנן's proof from a messenger sent to buy vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that a שליח sent for vegetables comes back with gourds and says 'I only found gourds,' which suggests gourds are not vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי עקיבא: When a person tells his messenger 'buy me vegetables,' doesn't the messenger come back and say 'I could only find gourds'? So gourds must be something other than vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן bring an everyday example to prove their side against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger apologizes: 'I found only gourds.' That sounds as if he did not find what he was sent for. So, the רבנן argue, people do not call gourds 'vegetables.'

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Akiva:
But doesn't a person say to his messenger
'Buy me vegetables,'
and he says: 'I found only gourds'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַהֲלֹא אוֹמֵר אָדָם לִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the first opinion of the משנה and challenges רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That דלועין are not included in ירק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: How a שליח sent to buy vegetables normally talks when he returns with gourds.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא turns the proof around
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the messenger would never say 'I only found legumes.' So the fact that he brings gourds shows that gourds do count as vegetables, while legumes do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Exactly! Would the messenger ever say 'I only found legumes'? No. So gourds are included in 'vegetables,' and legumes are not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא uses the same messenger example to prove his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gourds were a totally different food, the messenger would not buy them at all, just as he would never come back with legumes. The fact that he brings gourds shows they fall under 'vegetables,' even if they are a less typical kind. His apology only shows they are not the first choice.

keyTerms.meaning: that is exactly right / so it is

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not deny that the messenger apologizes. He agrees with the facts and reads them the other way: buying gourds at all shows they belong to the vegetable family.

phrases.english: He said to them: That is exactly so,
or does he perhaps say
'I found only legumes'?
Rather, this shows that gourds are included in vegetables,
and legumes are not included in vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם כֵּן הַדָּבָר אוֹ שֶׁמָּא אוֹמֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's proof by reading the same example in his own favor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The messenger's apology shows that gourds are not vegetables.
steps.terutzMaskana: A messenger only substitutes something from the same category. Since he would never bring legumes, bringing gourds shows they are inside the ירק category.

steps.title: Fresh versus dry Egyptian beans
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that one who vowed off ירק is forbidden fresh פול המצרי but may eat it dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is forbidden to eat fresh Egyptian beans, but he may eat dry ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new case: the same food can count as a vegetable when fresh and not when dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh, the bean is eaten like a vegetable, so the vow covers it. Dry, it is treated like a legume, which רבי עקיבא just said is not ירק, so it stays permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה: ירק includes דלועין according to רבי עקיבא, but never קטנית. Fresh Egyptian bean is ירק, and dry Egyptian bean is not.

phrases.english: And he is forbidden to eat the fresh Egyptian bean,
and permitted to eat the dry one.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against ירק forbids fresh פול המצרי and permits dry פול המצרי.

steps.title: How can a vow on vegetables include gourds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the person vowed off ירק, so how can that reach gourds?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who vows off vegetables, etc.' But he vowed off vegetables! Why should gourds be included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and immediately questions רבי עקיבא's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gourds seem to be a separate kind of food, not plain 'vegetables.' So it is hard to see how a vow using the word ירק could forbid them.

keyTerms.meaning: short for גמרא: the discussion of the משנה begins

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'One who vows off vegetables,' etc.
But he vowed off vegetables!
phrases.notes: This is aimed at רבי עקיבא: how can the word 'vegetables' stretch to cover gourds?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow named only ירק, and gourds seem to be a different food, so the vow should not cover them.

steps.title: עולא: he said 'pot vegetables'
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the case is where the person said 'pot vegetables are forbidden to me,' and gourds are cooked in a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The משנה is talking about someone who said 'Vegetables of the pot are forbidden to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge by narrowing what the person actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because gourds are cooked in a pot, the wording 'pot vegetables' could include them. That is why רבי עקיבא forbids them.

keyTerms.meaning: pot vegetables, vegetables of the cooking pot

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is where he says: 'Pot vegetables are forbidden to me,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר יַרְקֵי קְדֵרָה עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by redefining the wording of the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'pot vegetables,' a phrase that can include gourds.

steps.title: Maybe 'pot vegetables' means vegetables eaten with pot food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'pot vegetables' might mean vegetables eaten together with the pot food, which would not include gourds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he meant a vegetable that is eaten in a pot, one added to the pot to flavor the food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on עולא's wording, because it could have a narrower meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Pot vegetables' could mean vegetables added to the pot for flavor. Gourds would not fit that meaning, so the answer does not yet explain רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: But perhaps he means a vegetable that is eaten in a pot?
phrases.notes: He means a vegetable tossed into the pot to flavor the food, not one cooked as a dish of its own.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could mean only flavoring vegetables, which would leave gourds out.

steps.title: He said 'a vegetable cooked in a pot'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the case: he said 'a vegetable that is cooked in a pot,' which does include gourds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he says: 'A vegetable that is cooked in a pot is forbidden to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by making the wording of the vow more exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cooked in a pot' covers anything cooked there as its own dish, and gourds qualify. Now רבי עקיבא's ruling makes sense, and the רבנן still argue.

phrases.english: It is where he says: 'A vegetable that is cooked in a pot is forbidden to me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by sharpening the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Pot vegetables' might mean only flavoring vegetables.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'cooked in a pot,' and that wording can include gourds.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the גמרא, the dispute in the משנה is about a vow on 'a vegetable cooked in a pot.'

steps.title: What is the principle behind the dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic idea the רבנן and רבי עקיבא disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next step. The גמרא wants the underlying reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides used the same messenger example. Now the גמרא wants to state the general rule each side draws from it.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides the רבנן and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Does checking with the sender mean 'different kind' or 'same kind'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that if a שליח must ask before buying something, it is a different kind. רבי עקיבא holds that if a שליח asks about it, it is the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: anything a messenger needs to check with the sender about is not the same type. רבי עקיבא holds: anything a messenger checks about is the same type.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving each side's general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the messenger would ask before buying gourds. For the רבנן, needing to ask shows gourds are outside 'vegetables.' For רבי עקיבא, asking at all shows they are close enough to be included, because nobody asks about a totally different food like legumes.

keyTerms.meaning: to consult, to check with someone
its own kind, the same type

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a single food question into a general test for how far the wording of a vow reaches.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
Any item about which a messenger needs
to consult — is not the same type.
And Rabbi Akiva holds:
Any item about which a messenger consults —
is the same type.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי כֹּל מִילְּתָא דִּצְרִיךְ שְׁלִיחָא לְאִמְּלוֹכֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether an item a שליח must check about counts as outside the category (רבנן) or inside it (רבי עקיבא).
steps.whatToRemember: Same fact, opposite conclusions: the messenger checks before buying gourds. רבנן: so they are a different kind. רבי עקיבא: so they are the same kind.

steps.title: אביי: even רבי עקיבא gives no lashes
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even רבי עקיבא agrees that one who eats gourds after this vow does not receive מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי עקיבא agrees that, as far as lashes go, he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to רבי עקיבא's ruling: gourds are forbidden, but eating them does not bring lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא forbids gourds, yet he admits they are not a clear-cut part of 'vegetables,' since the messenger has to ask about them. Because the vow does not clearly cover them, the strict punishment of מלקות does not apply.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean gourds become permitted for רבי עקיבא. They stay forbidden. אביי only says the punishment of lashes does not apply.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi Akiva concedes with regard to lashes,
that he is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְעִנְיַן מַלְקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי עקיבא's ruling as just explained in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי עקיבא, one who eats gourds after vowing off 'a vegetable cooked in a pot' is not punished with מלקות.

steps.title: A משנה about a שליח who misuses הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מעילה. If the שליח did his job, the בעל הבית is guilty. If he did not do his job, the שליח is guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: if a שליח did what he was sent to do, the owner who sent him is guilty of מעילה. If he did not do what he was sent to do, the שליח himself is guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source from another מסכת. It is setting up a question about which תנא wrote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a שליח follows his orders, his action counts as the sender's action, so the sender is guilty. Once the שליח changes the orders, he is no longer acting as a שליח, so the action is his own. This connects to our topic of what counts as 'the same kind.'

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
An agent sent to do something for someone else
The owner, the one who sent the שליח
Is guilty of מעילה, using הקדש (holy property) for personal use

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת מעילה.

phrases.english: An agent who did his mission —
the owner has misused the holy property.
If he did not do his mission —
the agent has misused the holy property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test רבי עקיבא's rule from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who follows orders makes the בעל הבית guilty of מעילה. A שליח who changes orders is guilty himself.

steps.title: Who taught this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is the author of this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא of this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question matters because the answer depends on how you define 'his mission.' Whether the שליח changed his job depends on what counts as the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?

phrases.english: Who is the teacher of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the מעילה משנה follows.

steps.title: רב חסדא: not like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא. He shows this from the case of meat and liver, where the שליח is guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the משנה is not like רבי עקיבא. As we learned: How so? The owner told him, 'Give meat to the guests,' and he gave them liver. Or he said 'Give liver,' and he gave them meat. In these cases the שליח is guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He brings the משנה's own example: the שליח switched meat and liver, so the שליח is guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats liver and meat as different things. Because of that, switching them means the שליח did not do his mission. רב חסדא will now explain why that cannot fit רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
The משנה being discussed. Here it is the משנה in מעילה just quoted, not the משנה about vows.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The mishnah is not like Rabbi Akiva,
as we learned: How so?
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same משנה in מעילה, giving an example.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Give meat to the guests,'
and he gave them liver;
'Give liver,' and he gave them meat —
the agent has misused the holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי עקיבא, because it treats switching meat and liver as leaving the mission.

steps.title: Why it cannot be רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: If it were רבי עקיבא, he holds that anything a שליח would ask about is the same kind. So liver counts as meat, and the בעל הבית should be guilty, not the שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were רבי עקיבא, didn't רבי עקיבא say: anything a שליח would stop and ask about is the same kind? Then the owner should be guilty of מעילה, and the שליח should not be!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב חסדא's proof. It uses רבי עקיבא's rule to show that the משנה's ruling cannot match him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח sent for meat would ask, 'Should I bring liver?' According to רבי עקיבא from step 10, that makes liver the same kind as meat. Then the שליח did do his mission, so the בעל הבית should be guilty. The משנה says the שליח is guilty, so it must follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: That he would stop and ask about
Let him be guilty of מעילה

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: the מעילה משנה follows the רבנן. Under רבי עקיבא's rule, liver would count as meat, and the בעל הבית would be guilty.

phrases.english: And if it were Rabbi Akiva,
didn't Rabbi Akiva say:
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 10.

phrases.english: Anything an agent would stop and ask about —
is the same kind,
so let the owner be guilty of misuse
and let the agent not be guilty of misuse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב חסדא's claim in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the מעילה משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's rule that anything a שליח asks about is the same kind (step 10).

steps.title: אביי: it can even fit רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins to argue that the משנה could follow רבי עקיבא after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to push back on רב חסדא. This is a setup line, and his explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי disagrees with the claim that the משנה cannot be רבי עקיבא. He will need to explain why, even for רבי עקיבא, the שליח who switched meat and liver is guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers רב חסדא

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it is Rabbi Akiva,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to reject רב חסדא's conclusion from steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated here. אביי's reason comes on the next amud.
